title: Vector size transition — compatibility playbook and client migration plan
creator: Asha Patel
description: Plan and implement a safe rollout for changing the canonical embedding vector dimensionality used by the embeddings and reranking endpoints. This ticket defines compatibility shims, reindex strategies, SDK/API negotiation, performance/latency trade-offs, monitoring, and rollback procedures. Goal: enable a nominal size increase from 512->768 or decrease scenarios with minimal customer disruption and predictable SLO impact.
acceptance_criteria: API accepts and advertises embeddings.schema_version header and returns a stable version string
Server-side projection shim handles older client vectors and returns correct reranking results within acceptable delta
Dual-index aliasing works: new index built and validated in shadow mode before traffic switch
End-to-end latency regression <= 10% at p95 for rerank requests during normal load
Automated telemetry emits: dim_mismatch_rate, projection_fallback_rate, rerank_quality_delta, reindex_progress
Rollback to previous index/version can be executed within 15 minutes with automated routing revert
decisions: Adopt dual-index approach (old_index, new_index) and atomic alias switch for final cutover
Expose embeddings.schema_version in HTTP header and in SDK handshakes so clients can signal capability
Implement server-side linear projection when shrinking/expanding dims for short-term compatibility instead of requiring clients to re-emit vectors immediately
Perform quality validation via holdout reranking tests and human evals before traffic migration
Quantization profile recommendation: default to 8-bit symmetric quantization for larger dims to reduce storage/IO impact
implementation_steps: 1) Assessment: run job that samples top customer workloads to estimate dim growth impact on storage, index build time, and recall change
2) API/SDK: define schema_version header, update SDKs (py, js, go) to fetch schema_version and accept projection responses
3) Server shim: implement fast projection matrix path using a cached small matrix per model-version that maps legacy vectors -> new-dim space. Keep projection path quantized for speed.
4) Indexing: build new index in shadow mode using background reindexers. Tune HNSW parameters for new dimensionality and update disk layout throughput settings.
5) Validation: run automated rerank A/B with held-out queries comparing old vs new index; compute rerank_quality_delta and token-latency impact
6) Gradual traffic migration: route X% of queries using consistent hashing to new_index alias; monitor telemetry for regressions for 24-72 hours
7) Cutover: if metrics stable, perform alias atomic swap; notify customers and update docs
8) Post-cutover: schedule index consolidation, prune old indexes after retention window, and publish migration report
rollback_plan: If rerank_quality_delta exceeds threshold or p95 latency regresses >10% for >30 minutes, atomically revert alias to old_index, scale up background index build workers to catch up, and open incident channel. Telemetry will trigger an automated revert if soft-fallback hits exceed configured rate. Post-rollback, begin root-cause analysis and disable projection shim if it introduces noise.
risks: Projection matrix may introduce semantic drift for some models and workloads — mitigated via holdout tests and human review
Index rebuilds can impact IO and cluster capacity — mitigated by off-peak builds and autoscaling reserved workers
Clients that hardcode expected dimension in downstream services (search pipelines) may break — mitigate with SDK updates and customer comms
Long-running reindex jobs could fall behind if data churn high — mitigate with incremental reindexing and snapshotting
notes: Prefer incremental reindexing using time-partitioned snapshots for very large corpora to reduce rebuild windows.
Consider offering a temporary hosted projection API endpoint that clients can call to upgrade stored vectors in their own DBs (one-off tool).
Evaluate viability of storing canonical embeddings in a versioned blobstore + on-the-fly upscaling rather than immediate reindex for lower-cost customers.
